common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Viral (adenoviral) conjunctivitis / epidemic keratoconjunctivitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bacterial conjunctivitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Highly contagious — spread precautions needed.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Viral Conjunctivitis Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Viral Conjunctivitis Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis.
reference_soap.plan: Provide supportive care with preservative-free artificial tears and cool compresses; routine antibiotics are not indicated. Reinforce hand hygiene, avoidance of shared towels/cosmetics, and avoidance of contact lenses until resolved. Arrange ophthalmology assessment for pain, photophobia, reduced vision, corneal findings, or prolonged/severe symptoms.

teaching.one_liner: 29M post-URI with watery discharge, burning, redness starting in one eye and spreading to both, with tender preauricular node.
red_flags: Highly contagious; spread precautions are needed
Corneal involvement (subepithelial infiltrates) can develop later

must_ask.objective: Ask about recent upper respiratory infection
must_ask.say: Have you had a cold or sore throat recently?
Is the discharge watery, or thick and colored?

must_ask.objective: Ask about spread from one eye to the other
must_ask.say: Did it start in one eye and spread to the other?

must_ask.objective: Check for tender lymph node in front of the ear
must_ask.say: Do you feel a tender lump in front of your ear?
This is very contagious. Please wash your hands often and avoid sharing towels until it clears.
